summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with a dislodged nephrostomy tube, left flank pain, and signs of kidney infection. Imaging confirmed severe left hydroureteronephrosis due to tube dysfunction. He underwent successful nephrostomy tube exchange with secure fixation. He was treated with IV meropenem for pyelonephritis, though he declined the final IV dose and oral antibiotic initiation in the hospital. He was discharged with a prescription for oral fosfomycin to complete the course. His chronic left hip wound was monitored, and leg swelling was evaluated, revealing a subacute tibial fracture without need for intervention. Renal function remained stable, and he was discharged home with follow-up instructions for urology, orthopedics, and medication adherence.
problems: Infection of incontinent external stoma of urinary tract
Pressure ulcer of left hip, stage 4
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Other fracture of upper end of left tibia, subsequent encounter for closed fracture with routine healing
